identity.title: Electro-Acupuncture Decreases Postoperative Pain and Improves Recovery in Patients Undergoing a Supratentorial Craniotomy

source_review.full_publication: Read all 11 PDF pages including methods, results, discussion and references.
source_review.retrieval: Local full publication complete. PubMed DOI/title search https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25169910/ verified identity but did not establish trial registration or recruitment dates.

design.population: 88 adults, 18–60, ASA I–II, supratentorial tumor resection under general anesthesia; Beijing Tiantan Hospital. Needling-resistant patients excluded before enrollment.
design.comparator: No treatment / usual care; no needles, not sham
design.intervention: Ipsilateral LI4/SJ5, BL63/LR3, ST36/GB40; 2/100 Hz alternating every 3 s, maximum tolerance; after induction through end of surgery.
design.randomization: Computer-generated random-number table; concealment not reported.
design.blinding: Patients sedated before stimulation and explicitly unaware of allocation; postoperative assessor blinded; treating acupuncturist necessarily aware.
design.attrition: Seven excluded: two reoperations, two remaining unconscious and three incomplete data. Arm-specific reasons unavailable; 4/45 EA and 3/43 controls missing.

regimen.pca: 10 µg/kg fentanyl + 8 mg ondansetron in 100 mL, no basal infusion; bolus 1 mL, lockout 15 min, maximum 4 mL/h. Connected at end of surgery but activated following patient instruction in PACU; discontinued at 48 h.
regimen.rescue: Statistical methods mention rescue analgesic doses, but independent rescue regimen and contribution to total systemic opioid use are insufficiently reported.

independent_outcomes.qualification: Means are printed numerical point labels, not digitization. SD error bars have no numerical labels. Stars appear at 2/3/4/6 h; narrative generalizes first6h. No 24h or48h star.

independent_outcomes.window: Apparently postoperative course through 48 h; exact start and interval attribution not explicit in results
independent_outcomes.qualification: Authors say no difference, despite printed summaries giving a conventional independent-groups t near 2.54. Weight-dependent 100mL bag and roughly10/15 effective 1mL boluses suggest a further order-of-magnitude dose-accounting inconsistency. Do not change printed units or infer mass from mean weight.

independent_outcomes.window: First postoperative day (abstract describes within first24h; confirm clock)
independent_outcomes.qualification: Counts reconstructed unambiguously from rounded percentages and denominators. Abstract incorrectly claims P<0.05.
Ordinal appetite recovery, not validated QoR or time-to-first GI event.

opioid_candidate.reason: No cumulative exact0–24h mass. Reported total fentanyl apparently48h and internally inconsistent with dosing account; weight-dependent PCIA counts cannot be converted via group mean weight.

independence: Distinct supplied publication. Same center and several investigators/acupoints as cited An2010a/b and Yang2012; paper calls them previous studies, but no recruitment dates or registry identifier establishes participant nonoverlap. Do not assume duplicate solely from authorship; unresolved author check.

1.2: Allocation concealment mechanism is not described.
1.3: Baseline only for81 completers; tumor histology differs between arms, but no firm evidence that randomization failed.
2.1: Participants were sedated before EA and explicitly unaware of allocation.
2.2: Acupuncturist delivered needles versus no needles.
2.3: Same GA and PCIA protocol; no trial-context departures reported.
2.6: Analyzed according to assigned arm among participants with outcomes. Clinical missingness belongs in D3; no crossover or nonadherence exclusions reported.
2.7: No separate inappropriate as-treated analysis established.
3.2: No sensitivity analysis for seven excluded patients.
3.3: Reoperation and persistent unconsciousness can be strongly associated with postoperative pain, opioid needs and complications.
3.4: Explicit clinical-recovery exclusions make outcome-dependent missingness likely, although arm-specific reasons are absent.
4.1: Standard resting0–10VAS measured at scheduled times.
4.2: Same schedule and single blinded assessor asked standardized questions.
4.3: Self-rating participants and postoperative observer reported unaware of EA, delivered under GA.
5.1: No registration identifier or dated prospective SAP in the full report; targeted DOI search did not establish one.
5.2: Multiple scheduled pain times and recovery outcomes; precise prospective endpoint selection unavailable.
5.3: Multiple PCIA periods/definitions and tests; no dated SAP.

rob_independent.reason: Clinically related post-randomization missingness can bias recovery outcomes; low D4 is supported by intervention under GA and blinded postoperative assessment, not merely the label double-blind.
